coverage_limits: Adoption behavior under an operator-confirmation requirement is unobserved, and NO instrument currently planned can observe it: the es#166 window measures envelope adoption generally and cannot see a mechanism that does not exist. Observing it requires a bounded pilot in which the mechanism is actually available (see empirical_closure and recovery_moves).

Principal binding is outside the contract (SECURITY.md): the contract cannot verify that a human rather than an agent authored an operator-confirmed grant. This limit bounds every option here equally.

SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-14 first issue, whose empirical closure was VACUOUS: it predicted that no mission would adopt a field that cannot exist under this record's own validity condition. A prediction true by construction is not evidence, and the synthesis had named that test as the route to closing the authorship question.

rigor.trigger: a single proposed design needs correctness confirmation or reversal
rigor.tier_reason: the conclusion mandates a persistent authority model on a security boundary; focused forbids selection or reversal of a persistent design

decision_frame.question: Under which authorship model can grants_paths deliver the property it is proposed for: operator-confirmed, or steward-authored with operator visibility?
decision_frame.system_boundary: mission-custody grants_paths as proposed in es#150, prior to any implementation; the authority relation between steward_ref (agent) and operator_ref (human).

alternatives.description: Defer the authorship decision; grants_paths stays blocked.
Operator-confirmed: a grant is not live until the operator confirms it.
Steward-authored, operator-visible: the steward writes grants; they are recorded and surfaced but not blocked on the operator.

hard_constraints: grants_paths must be a CONTROL in the README's own taxonomy, not a DECLARATION — that is the stated reason for proposing it.
No actor certifies its own acceptance (contract acceptance-tier doctrine).
authorized_objectives: Give effect-shaped missions a machine-checkable boundary (es#166 finding).
Do not widen what a steward may do without the operator's authority (acceptance-table re-derivation: permission is not authority because effects happen indirectly).
empirical_premises: Stewards populate envelope fields when doing so fits the work shape, and leave them empty when it does not (es#166 measured finding).

coverage.reason: Whether a grant bounds the granted party is a safety property of the authority relation, not only an access-control detail.
No representation or dependency question bears load; the field shape is not at issue here.
No ordering, isolation or concurrency property bears load on authorship.
No replicated or distributed state inside the declared boundary.
No fault or recovery property bears load on who authors a grant.
This is the authority question directly: whether the constrained party may author its own constraint.
No resource or capacity bound bears load.
No probabilistic or measurement claim bears load on the authorship relation itself; the adoption premise is handled as empirical closure.
The choice governs a lifecycle precondition for shipping grants_paths under an authorized constraint rule.

derivations.construct: a constraint authored by the constrained party is not a constraint on it
derivations.model: Authority relation between principal O (operator, human) and principal S (steward, agent). A grant G bounds which paths S may affect. Ask whether G constrains S.

preconditions.statement: steward_ref denotes an agent, and it is the steward that performs effects.
Under option B, S is the author of G and no other principal's assent is required for G to be live.
grants_paths is proposed in order to be a CONTROL rather than a DECLARATION.

fact_mapping.anchor: option B as stated in this frame

plugins/epistemic-skills/contracts/mission-custody/README.md@0fee7a0f59bdc5aac9ab6b4b2ee581d8e6c8b232 CONTROL/DECLARATION table; the scope row records that the existing control is 'a control against FORGETTING, not against intent'

steps: Under B, S may at any time author a grant that widens the paths S may affect, with no assent from O required for it to take effect.
A bound that the bounded party may unilaterally rewrite restricts that party only insofar as it chooses to be restricted.
That is precisely the property the README already ascribes to the existing scope machinery: a control against forgetting, not against intent.
grants_paths is proposed to be stronger than the existing machinery (p3); under B it is not stronger, it is the same class re-spelled.
Therefore B cannot satisfy the hard constraint that grants_paths be a CONTROL.

result.statement: Steward-authored grants_paths (option B) cannot deliver the property for which grants_paths is proposed; it reduces to a DECLARATION in the contract's own taxonomy.

derivations.counterexample: A steward whose instruction forbids writing outside src/ authors grants_paths: ['**'] in the same session and proceeds; every subsequent write is inside the declared grant, the record is self-consistent, and an auditor reading the manifest alone sees no crossing.
residual_mismatch: B retains audit value: the grant is recorded and comparable after the fact. The derivation refutes B as a control, not as a disclosure.

derivations.construct: a refutation of one option does not establish its complement
derivations.model: Two authorized objectives: give effect-shaped missions a machine-checkable boundary; do not widen steward authority without operator authority. Option A satisfies the second by construction. Ask whether it satisfies the first.

preconditions.statement: Envelope fields are populated when doing so fits the work shape and left empty when it does not.
A per-grant operator confirmation imposes strictly more steward-side friction than leaving a field empty.

fact_mapping.anchor: https://github.com/ZMS-Labs/epistemic-skills/issues/166 — scope.in, scope.out, permissions, protected_state all empty on media-library-rebuild (90 checkpoints, 9 receipts), populated on the file-shaped custody-instrument mission
option A as stated in this frame

steps: es#166 measured that the envelope is abandoned exactly where using it is inconvenient for the work shape.
Option A raises the cost of using the mechanism above that of the fields already measured as abandoned.
So the predicted outcome under A is non-adoption: grants_paths present in the schema and empty in practice, reproducing es#166 one field further on.
Non-adoption satisfies the authority objective vacuously while failing the boundary objective.
Whether A actually fails this way is an adoption question about human and agent behavior, which no derivation settles.

result.statement: Option A satisfies the authority objective but its satisfaction of the boundary objective is unresolved and depends on adoption behavior that has not been observed.

residual_mismatch: A batching or standing-grant form of A (operator confirms a class of grants once, not each grant) is a third alternative this frame did not enumerate and which may dominate A on friction; it is not evaluated here.

tests.belief: An operator-confirmation requirement suppresses use of the mechanism.
tests.test: BLOCKED. This record's own validity condition is grants_paths-remains-unshipped, so no mission can adopt a confirmation-gated field and 'no mission adopts one' is true by construction. Adoption of unrelated high-friction declarations is a proxy that cannot separate rejection of operator-confirmed grants from ordinary envelope behavior. A discriminating observation requires the mechanism to exist: a bounded pilot on one mission, which is a separate authorization.

basis: d1 refutes option B against a hard constraint: a steward-authored grant is a declaration, and grants_paths is proposed precisely to be more than a declaration.
d2 shows the refutation of B does not establish A: A satisfies the authority objective but its satisfaction of the boundary objective turns on unobserved adoption behavior.

The authorship question therefore stays OPEN, and not pending on the es#166 window: that window measures envelope adoption generally and cannot observe a mechanism that does not exist, so waiting on it would repeat the vacuity this record was corrected for. Closing it requires a bounded pilot (see recovery_moves), which is a separate authorization.
conditions: B may still be used as a disclosure mechanism; it may not be called a control.
concessions: Principal binding is outside the contract, so even option A cannot verify a human authored the confirmation; A improves the authority relation without closing it.
A batching/standing-grant variant was not evaluated and may dominate A.
recovery_moves: Record the reversal on B now, so the authorship precondition is partially discharged.
Enumerate the standing-grant variant (operator confirms a CLASS of grants once) as a third alternative before any authorship decision closes.

Authorize a BOUNDED PILOT of at least one authorship mechanism if the question must close: with grants_paths unshipped, no observation can discriminate the alternatives, so the question stays open by construction rather than by evidence.
Re-fire this derivation against pilot data, not against the es#166 window, which measures envelope adoption generally and cannot speak to a mechanism that does not exist.
